values.data_quality.bucket.Circular_mapping_mut: Two or more funds own each other in a loop. The engine resolves it by fixed-point so totals still reconcile, but a circular holding is a structural/data red flag that should be confirmed.
values.data_quality.bucket.Incomplete_look-thro: An intra-group holding is flagged to be eliminated on look-through (double-count = Y), but the target entity has no underlying positions to look through to (e.g. an opco shell). Its value can't be decomposed.
values.data_quality.bucket.Missing_dangling_SPV: A holding maps (via SPV Fund Code) to an entity that has no positions anywhere in the file. The look-through dead-ends — likely a missing feed or an incorrect SPV code.
values.data_quality.bucket.Self-mapping_fund_ho: A fund is recorded as a holder of its own SPV code (treasury / self-class). Excluded from the ownership math so it can't distort percentages, but flagged as a mapping/setup artifact to review.
values.data_quality.bucket.Unmapped_identifiers: An entity is referenced but has no VPM symbol and/or no name, so it can't be identified cleanly in downstream systems. A naming/reference-data gap.

values.glossary.intro: Every term used in TRACE-Pro, in plain language — with its SOURCE (which report/system the number comes from) and METHOD (how it is calculated). Start with the three price columns below if you are unsure why there are three.
values.glossary.section_headers: The three price columns — start here
values.glossary.term.allocation_tracker.definit: The reference that governs how a fund’s units are split across its parents (the allocation of ownership). It is what co-owned funds are checked against.
values.glossary.term.apex_fund_feeder_terminal_: An apex fund is a top-of-structure feeder the product holds directly (nothing above it inside the product); its NAV sums to the Product NAV. A terminal fund is the deepest end — no priced children — so it prices straight at NAV ÷ units and repricing starts there.
values.glossary.term.applied_effective_ownershi: The fraction of a node’s full value that ultimately belongs to the product, after multiplying ownership down every level of the chain. It is what rolls a node’s MV up to the product without double-counting.
values.glossary.term.before_vs_after_pricing.de: A global view toggle (top-right). Before = today’s as-booked reality (current marks, Derived MV, pricing gap open). After = the ideal fully-repriced state (every holding at its revised price; pricing gap ≈ $0). It changes several column labels: Current px→Applied px, Derived MV→Repriced MV, Repricing P&L→P&L (reconciled).
values.glossary.term.bps.definition: The size of a gap expressed relative to NAV, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). It lets you compare a dollar gap across funds of very different sizes; the flag chip turns amber at ≥25 bps and red at ≥50 bps.
values.glossary.term.carried_mv_position_mv.def: The market value at which a fund is carried on its holders’ books — the “Current MV of positions” line, i.e. what the position is booked at before any repricing.
When more than one parent holds the same fund. Each parent’s share is its ownership %, and the shares sum to ~100%.
values.glossary.term.current_px_applied_px.defi: The price the position is actually being valued at in the current view. In the Before view it is today’s as-booked mark; the same column is relabelled Applied px in the After view and then shows the revised price. That label-swap (Current → Applied) is the usual source of confusion — it is one column, two labels.
values.glossary.term.derived_mv_repriced_mv.def: The look-through market value of a fund — the sum of everything it owns, valued at today’s marks and weighted by ownership at each level. In the After view the column is relabelled Repriced MV and shows the same node at revised prices.
values.glossary.term.double_count.definition: The error of adding up NAVs that already contain each other — summing every fund’s NAV counts a parent and its children, hugely overstating the total. TRACE-Pro avoids it by summing only apex funds and by looking through with ownership %.
values.glossary.term.exception_break.definition: A fund flagged because a gap is material. A pricing break specifically means Publish px (NAV ÷ units) disagrees with the bottom-up Revised px.
values.glossary.term.fund_code.definition: The short code that identifies a fund or SPV (e.g. SPORTHFCSPV, DEUCE2FC). It is the join key between the Position Report and the NAV Report.
values.glossary.term.global_units_global_quanti: The total number of units of a fund in issue across all holders — the denominator for every per-unit price.
values.glossary.term.look_through.definition: Tracing a fund’s value down through every SPV and holding to the ultimate securities, weighting by ownership at each step, so you can value and attribute the fund from what it actually owns.
values.glossary.term.missing_linked_security.de: A holding that points to a linked fund / SPV code the source files cannot resolve — either the SPV code has no positions beneath it (nothing to look through) or the fund has no ENDING_NAV. Surfaced in the Issue Log.
values.glossary.term.nav.definition: A fund’s net asset value — assets minus liabilities — as reported. It is the source of truth for the publish price.
values.glossary.term.nav_report.definition: The .csv that supplies each fund’s NAV — the source of truth for prices and the Product NAV.
values.glossary.term.non_position.definition: The part of NAV that is not in the positions file at all — cash, fees payable, receivables. It is what remains after repricing reconciles the positions; it is not a pricing break.
values.glossary.term.other_non_position_compone: The same idea at the single-fund level — the slice of a fund’s NAV not represented by its positions (cash / fees / receivables).
values.glossary.term.ownership_immediate.defini: A holder’s direct share of a fund — how much of the child’s units this one parent holds. It is the % pill on each Structure / Simulator edge.
values.glossary.term.position_report.definition: The .xlsx that defines the structure and units — who holds what, how many units, and the ultimate securities.
values.glossary.term.pricing.definition: The product-level pricing adjustment — how much value moves when you reprice everything bottom-up to NAV, versus today’s marks.
values.glossary.term.product_nav.definition: The product’s own NAV — the sum of the NAVs of its top (“apex” / feeder) funds only. It is not the sum of every fund’s NAV.
values.glossary.term.publish_px.definition: The official unit price to publish for the day — what one unit is worth using the fund’s own reported NAV. It is the emphasised column and does not change between the Before and After views.
values.glossary.term.publish_px_vs_current_appl: The Look-Through Pricing table shows three unit prices for the same fund because each answers a different question: Publish = the price to send today (top-down from NAV); Current / Applied = the price the position is being valued at in the view you are on; Revised = the price rebuilt bottom-up from the underlyings. When Publish and Revised disagree, you are looking at a pricing break.
values.glossary.term.reconciled.definition: A level is reconciled when its pricing gap is ~$0 — the revised value equals the derived value, so no pricing break remains. Shown as $0 / green in the After view.
values.glossary.term.repricing_p_l_p_l_reconcil: The value change from repricing this fund’s holdings to their revised prices — Revised MV minus Derived MV. In the After view every level reconciles, so this column reads $0 and is relabelled “P&L (reconciled)”.
values.glossary.term.revised_mv.definition: The fund’s market value after bottom-up NAV repricing — every child valued at its revised price instead of its current mark.
values.glossary.term.revised_px.definition: The bottom-up NAV-repriced unit price. Built from the deepest funds upward: each terminal fund prices at NAV ÷ units, then every holder is revalued using its children’s revised prices. Always shown in its own column, in both views.
values.glossary.term.spv.definition: A special-purpose vehicle / holding entity that sits between a feeder and the ultimate assets. In the Structure graph these are the intermediate “SPV / holding” nodes.
values.glossary.term.the_additive_reconciliatio: TRACE-Pro reconciles the product with one additive chain: Derived MV + Δ Pricing = Revised MV, then + Δ Non-position = NAV. Nothing is recomputed by the Before/After toggle — it only switches which pre-computed set is shown — and Product NAV is untouched.
values.glossary.term.value_of_100_mv100.definit: The full market value of a node as if you owned 100% of it, before applying ownership. Node size on the Structure graph is proportional to this.
values.glossary.term.variance.definition: A general term for the difference between two views of the same value. The tool names the specific ones: Repricing P&L (Revised − Derived), Δ Non-position (NAV − Revised), and the price Diff P.U. (Current − Revised px).
values.glossary.term.vpm.definition: The accounting / valuation system the symbols and quantities come from — hence “Quantity VPM” and “VPM symbol”.
values.glossary.term.vpm_symbol.definition: The trading / accounting symbol for a fund or SPV (e.g. “SPORTHFCSPV”), from the VPM accounting system. Shown in the Symbol column.

values.pricing.banner.narrative: Bottom-up repricing Reprice the deepest funds first — a terminal fund's revised price = NAV ÷ units; a holder's revised MV = Σ held-qty × child revised price + its direct securities, propagated to the product. That lifts Derived $2,060,224,441 to Revised $2,060,610,338 (repricing P&L $385,897), then non-position items bridge to NAV $2,062,198,836. Largest repricing tier: SPORT ($336,038 across its 9 holdings). Click any fund for its per-holding P&L.
